expected_value: The exclusive mechanism is a reference under Paragraph 11 of the Advocates (Remuneration Orders) Rules (ARO). Invoking general rules of procedure is insufficient because it would defeat the special procedures enacted under Paragraph 11 of the Advocates Remuneration Order [chunk_id: Kariithi v GN Thiongo Associates (Miscellaneous Application E262of2025) 2026KEHC11082(KLR) (22July2026) (Ruling)__s2__c3].
correctness_reasoning: The answer correctly identifies a Paragraph 11 reference under the Advocates Remuneration Order as the exclusive mechanism and explains that general procedural rules cannot be used because the taxation process is governed by that special regime.
faithfulness_reasoning: The answer is directly supported by the context, which states that any challenge to a taxing officer’s decision on an item in an Advocates-Client bill of costs can only be made by a reference under Paragraph 11 of the Advocates Remuneration Order, and that invoking general procedural rules is insufficient because it would defeat the special statutory procedure.
